nodes.label: AEC Workflow Fragmentation
nodes.description: Disconnected drawings, calculations, estimates and construction records create repeated entry, inconsistency and weak traceability in Nepalese AEC workflows.

nodes.label: Research Question
nodes.description: The study asks how normalized shared AEC data can support reuse, traceable structural calculation and prototype validation.

nodes.label: Research Objectives
nodes.description: Seven specific objectives cover schema design, shared data, MDM, reuse, documentation linkage, health checks and evaluation.

nodes.label: Methodology
nodes.description: Prototype-based database design and implementation using PostgreSQL/Supabase exports and a controlled two-span beam example.

nodes.label: Normalized Relational Database
nodes.description: The normalized PostgreSQL relational model is the deterministic source of truth for the implemented prototype.

nodes.label: Shared Element Hub
nodes.description: Project elements, points, dimensions, parameters and units are stored once for reuse across selected workflows.

nodes.label: Structural Analysis
nodes.description: The implemented structural validation is the Moment Distribution Method for a controlled two-span beam; it is not a general analysis engine.

nodes.label: Architecture Representation
nodes.description: Two architecture line elements are generated from the shared A-B-C geometry in the verified export.

nodes.label: Quantity Estimation
nodes.description: Beam concrete volumes are calculated from shared length, breadth and depth values using the supplied quantity rule.

nodes.label: Construction Documentation
nodes.description: Elements are linked to construction work items, method-statement steps and specification clauses in the verified static exports.

nodes.label: Validation
nodes.description: Exported reporting views check joint equilibrium, convergence, duplicate stiffness locations and traceability within the implemented prototype.

nodes.label: Evidence
nodes.description: Public-safe exports and sanitized screenshots corroborate the displayed implementation results; the verified data remain authoritative.

nodes.label: Conclusions
nodes.description: The prototype demonstrates reuse of normalized data across selected AEC workflows and establishes a foundation for later integrations.

nodes.label: Limitations
nodes.description: The controlled beam prototype is not a complete building model, commercial BIM-GIS platform or replacement for advanced engineering software.

nodes.label: Future Scope
nodes.description: Full IFC, PostGIS, code checking, scheduling, BOQ, procurement and controlled AI interfaces remain future work.

nodes.label: Thesis
nodes.description: The MSc study of a normalized relational database supporting selected BIM/GIS-oriented AEC workflow automation in Nepal.

nodes.label: AEC Workflow Fragmentation
nodes.description: Repeated entry and disconnected discipline files are the problem addressed by the prototype.

nodes.label: Research Question
nodes.description: Five research questions address schema design, shared reuse, BIM/GIS concepts, structural traceability and validation.

nodes.label: Research Objectives
nodes.description: The general and seven specific objectives define the implemented prototype scope and evaluation.

nodes.label: Methodology
nodes.description: Prototype-based database design, implementation, controlled testing and query-based validation.

nodes.label: Prototype Validation
nodes.description: Validation uses exported consistency, traceability, quantity, convergence and health-check evidence.

nodes.label: Conclusion
nodes.description: Normalized data can serve as a backbone for the selected demonstrated workflows within the stated limits.

nodes.label: Limitations
nodes.description: The sample is controlled and beam-based; advanced analysis, full BIM/GIS and production modules are outside the implementation.

nodes.label: Future Scope
nodes.description: The thesis proposes expansion to full building, BIM/GIS, scheduling, procurement and controlled AI capabilities.
